summary: Consolidate legacy Confluence spaces into topic-hub and provide permission-translation bot
description: Issue summary: We have ~18 legacy Confluence spaces created over multiple years for various experiment pods and research projects. These spaces have overlapping topics, inconsistent permission models (individuals added to page-level groups, expired service accounts, and external guest users), and duplicate content. Impact: Searchability is poor, audits for compliance are noisy, and new team members cannot find canonical guidance. This creates risk for compliance-heavy projects that need strict ownership and retention rules. Background: Past attempts to manually merge spaces caused page permission regressions and lost edit history. Request: Create a migration plan to consolidate legacy spaces into a smaller set of topic-hub spaces, implement a permission-translation bot that maps page-level permissions to space-level groups where possible, and produce a one-click rollback plan. Include an archival policy for low-value pages and a content-owner verification flow for all merged pages. Acceptance criteria: - Target topic-hub spaces created with appropriate templates - Bot translates at least 90% of page-level permissions to space-level groups without granting broader access than original pages - Migration preserves page history and attachments - Content owners notified and given 7 days to review/opt-out before final archive - Documented rollback and post-migration audit checklist
migration_steps: Inventory: run Confluence space audit and produce CSV of spaces, page counts, contributors, and explicit permissions
Mapping: propose mapping from legacy spaces to topic-hub destinations and owner contacts
Dry-run: run permission-translation bot in dry-run mode on a small pilot space and validate no access escalation
Pilot: migrate 2 pilot spaces (research-experiments, inference-evals) to the topic-hub and run owner reviews
Full-run: schedule phased migration windows for remaining spaces with pre-migration backups
Archive: apply archival templates to pages flagged as low-value and set retention metadata
Audit: run post-migration access reports and reconcile with dry-run outputs
Rollback: if critical issues found, restore from backup and rollback bot changes
acceptance_criteria: Permission delta shows no increase in unique users with edit rights post-migration
All migrated pages retain edit history and attachments
>90% of explicit page permissions mapped to reusable groups
Content owners confirmed within 7 days or pages flagged for team review
Post-migration audit report published to Confluence and linked in ticket
risks: Permission translation may miss custom page macros that reference user lists
External guest accounts could be granted unintended access if translation is naive
Large attachments could impact migration duration and require temporary increased quota
Owners not responding could delay migration windows
rollout_plan: Week 0: Audit and mapping, stakeholder review
Week 1: Build and test permission-translation bot in staging
Week 2: Dry-run on pilot space with SRE and Security watching
Week 3: Pilot migrations and owner verification
Weeks 4-6: Phased migrations (2-3 spaces per week) with nightly backups
Week 7: Final audit and close ticket
